capabilities: Sync bank accounts through SimpleFIN Bridge via ribbon, command palette, settings or on startup
Reconcile late-posting and pending charges without duplicating transactions
Store accounts and transactions as JSON with optional CSV copies in a chosen folder layout
Expose an api.v1 with a sync-completed event and TypeScript types for scripts and plugins
Sync made-up demo data with no account or network use
extras: The plugin is unreviewed by Obsidian staff. Real bank data needs a paid SimpleFIN Bridge account (about $15/year); demo mode works with no account. The README warns that Obsidian does not isolate secret storage between plugins and points to docs/threat-model.md for security details.
intentEvidence: PassBook is a data layer: sync with one command, then build your own notes, daily summaries, dashboards and scripts on top.
problem: Obsidian has no way to import banking data, so tracking accounts and transactions in notes means manual entry or ad-hoc exports.

relations.evidence: Syncs your accounts through SimpleFIN Bridge: link your banks there once, paste one setup token into PassBook

summary: Pulls bank and credit card accounts, balances and transactions into the vault as JSON and CSV via SimpleFIN Bridge, with an API for scripts.
